title: Finite constant groups on projective curve families
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a projective
morphism of finite-type
schemes over a field, with geometric fibre dimensions at most one.
If the order of a finite abelian group $M$ is invertible on $S$,
every higher direct image
$R^qf_*\underline M$ is
constructible.

proof.text: Fix $n=|M|\ge1$ and the morphism $f$. All sheaves and higher direct images in this argument are abelian sheaves on the small etale sites. The source category has enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives], and $f_*$ is additive and left exact by [lem-weil-pbc-direct-image-left-exact]. By [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], $R^qf_*F=\mathcal H^q(Rf_*F)$ with $Rf_*F\cong Q(f_*I)$ for every K-injective resolution $F\to I$; an injective resolution $I$ of $F$ concentrated in degrees $\ge0$ is K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative] (2), so $R^qf_*F\cong H^q(f_*I)$, the right derived functor of $f_*$ computed by injective resolutions. Constructibility is invariant under isomorphism, so we may work with the latter. Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-horseshoe-delta-functor] (2) applies: the $R^qf_*$ are additive functors and give a long exact sequence for every short exact sequence. We prove, by strong induction on $|N|$, that every $R^qf_*\underline N$, $q\ge0$, is constructible for each finite abelian group $N$ whose order divides $n$. For $N=0$, its constant sheaf is zero and every derived image is zero: an additive functor sends the zero identity to zero, so its value on the zero object is a zero object. The zero sheaf is finite constant, hence constructible by [def-weil-pbc-constructible-abelian-sheaf].

For nonzero $N$, choose $x\ne0$, let $d>1$ be its least positive period, and choose a prime $\ell\mid d$. Division with remainder shows that $a x=0$ exactly when $d\mid a$; hence $y=(d/\ell)x$ has order exactly $\ell$. Thus $H=\langle y\rangle\cong\mathbf F_\ell$ as an additive group. Translation identifies every coset of $H$ with $H$, so counting the disjoint cosets gives $|N|=\ell|Q|$ for $Q=N/H$. Therefore $|Q|<|N|$, and both $\ell$ and $|Q|$ divide $n$. If $n=\ell a$, then $a n^{-1}$ is an inverse to $\ell$ in every local ring of $S$, so $\ell$ is invertible on $S$. This produces $0\to H\to N\to Q\to0$ and is precisely one step of the finite prime-factor filtration in the blueprint; repeating on $Q$ terminates because its cardinality decreases.

The constant presheaves associated with $0\to H\to N\to Q\to0$ are sectionwise short exact. By [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] their sheafifications are the associated constant abelian sheaves. The exactness of abelian sheafification in [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact] (2) therefore gives $0\to\underline H\to\underline N\to\underline Q\to0$ on $X_{\Et}$. This is the exactness asserted by Stacks 093J (lemma-constant-exact); no splitting as groups is assumed.

source.place: Tag 093J, lemma-constant-exact, statement and first sentence of proof; Sites Tag 00WJ, lemma-sheafification-exact

proof.text: Apply [thm-fin-projective-curve-constant] to $f$ and $\ell$. Its projectivity, finite-type-over-a-field and geometric-fibre-dimension hypotheses are unchanged, and step 2 supplies the required invertibility. That node is stated for the constant sheaf of $\mathbf F_\ell$-modules, its higher direct images in $\Mod(\,\cdot_{\Et},\mathbf F_\ell)$, and constructibility as sheaves of $\mathbf F_\ell$-modules [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]; it gives a constructible $\mathbf F_\ell$-module sheaf $G_q=R^qf_*\underline{\mathbf F_\ell}$. We transport this to the abelian setting of step 1. (a) The underlying abelian sheaf of the constant $\mathbf F_\ell$-module sheaf is the constant abelian sheaf $\underline{\mathbf F_\ell}$: both are the sheafification of the same constant presheaf, and by [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] the sheafification of a presheaf of modules has the abelian sheafification as underlying abelian sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. (b) By [lem-sbc-higher-direct-image-forget-comparison], the underlying abelian sheaf of $G_q$ is isomorphic to the abelian $R^qf_*\underline{\mathbf F_\ell}$ of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. (c) Forgetting scalars preserves constructibility: take the stratification $(\iota_k)$ witnessing [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf] for $G_q$; by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] (2) the module inverse images along $\iota_k$ and then along the members $U_i\to Z_k$ of the trivializing covers have the abelian inverse images as underlying abelian sheaves, the module isomorphisms to $\underline{M_i}$ forget to abelian isomorphisms, and by (a) for the finite module $M_i$ the underlying abelian sheaf of $\underline{M_i}$ is the constant abelian sheaf on the finite group $M_i$. So the same strata and covers witness [def-weil-pbc-constructible-abelian-sheaf], and all abelian $R^qf_*\underline{\mathbf F_\ell}$ are constructible.

source.place: Proof, prime-factor induction ('starting from [thm-fin-projective-curve-constant]'); coefficient comparison as in Stacks 03RW (2),(3)

proof.text: Since the chosen additive isomorphism $H\cong\mathbf F_\ell$ induces an isomorphism of constant abelian sheaves, hence of their abelian higher direct images, all $R^qf_*\underline H$ are constructible. The inductive hypothesis applies to $Q$ by step 2 and gives constructibility of all $R^qf_*\underline Q$. The induction is simultaneous in every degree, so it supplies the terms in degrees $q$ and $q+1$, and in degree $q-1$ when $q>0$, needed below; the degree $-1$ boundary is treated separately in step 7.

source.place: Proof, 'Proceed by induction along this filtration'

proof.text: Set $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/n$. Each of $H,N,Q$ is killed by $n$: for any element $z$ of a finite group $P$ of order dividing $n$, its cyclic subgroup has size equal to its least positive period $e$, and counting its cosets gives $e\mid|P|\mid n$, hence $nz=0$. Hence $n\,\mathrm{id}=0$ on the constant presheaf with value $P$, and on its sheafification $\underline P$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], sheafification being exact and so additive by [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact] (2). Additivity from [lem-weil-pbc-horseshoe-delta-functor] (2) gives $n\,\mathrm{id}_{R^qf_*\underline P}=R^qf_*(n\,\mathrm{id}_{\underline P})=0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-sheaves-killed-by-n-zmod-modules] (2),(3), all these sheaves have unique $\Lambda_S$-module structures and every abelian map between them is $\Lambda_S$-linear. By [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-abelian-zn-module-constructible], the constructible abelian sheaves $R^qf_*\underline H$ and $R^qf_*\underline Q$ of step 5 (all $q$) are, on $S$ and with this structure, constructible sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf], with the same underlying abelian sheaf.

source.place: Definition 03RW (definition-constructible), parts (2),(3); the comparison is the cited node lem-weil-pbc-constructible-abelian-zn-module-constructible

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact] to step 3, with the hypotheses checked in step 1. For a fixed $q\ge0$, write $A=R^qf_*\underline H$, $B=R^qf_*\underline N$, $C=R^qf_*\underline Q$ and $D=R^{q+1}f_*\underline H$. For $q>0$ put $T=R^{q-1}f_*\underline Q$; for $q=0$ put $T=0$, using the initial $0\to f_*\underline H\to f_*\underline N$ of the long exact sequence. Its exact segment $T\xrightarrow u A\xrightarrow v B\xrightarrow w C\xrightarrow z D$ gives $0\to\operatorname{coker}u\to B\to\ker z\to0$: $\ker v=\operatorname{im}u$ makes the map from $A/\operatorname{im}u$ injective with image $\operatorname{im}v=\ker w$, and $\operatorname{im}w=\ker z$ makes the map to $\ker z$ surjective. These are also the module kernel and cokernel and a module short exact sequence: by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], kernels are sectionwise and cokernels are sheafified sectionwise quotients with inherited scalar action, so their underlying abelian objects are precisely those just computed. All arrows are linear by step 6.

source.place: Tag 015B, lemma-higher-derived-functors (1),(2); elementary image/kernel calculation from the exact segment

proof.text: The ring $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/n$ is finite and commutative, including $n=1$. In step 7, $T,A,C,D$ are constructible $\Lambda_S$-module sheaves by steps 4, 5 and 6 (and $T=0$ when $q=0$). Apply [thm-constructible-serre] (1) to $u:T\to A$ and $z:C\to D$: their cokernel and kernel are constructible. Clause (2) applied to the short exact sequence of step 7 then makes $B$ constructible as a $\Lambda_S$-module sheaf. Forgetting scalars gives constructibility of the underlying abelian sheaf $B$ by the argument (c) of step 4: [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] (2) for the inverse images, and [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] for the underlying abelian sheaves of the finite constant module models, in [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf] and [def-weil-pbc-constructible-abelian-sheaf]. This finishes the induction for every $q\ge0$. Taking $N=M$ proves the item. If negative degrees are included in the notation, they vanish: use an injective resolution concentrated in nonnegative degrees in the definition [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], whose image under $f_*$ is still concentrated in those degrees.
